title: Writing
summary: Three tasks in 60 minutes, marked out of 20 by trained examiners. You need **10/20** for NCLC 7. It's the most template-friendly section: a fixed plan for each task, practised until it needs no thought, gets you most of the way.
facts: 60 minutes for all three tasks — you manage the time
**60–120 words** · a message: describe, tell or explain to a named reader (friend, neighbour, manager)
**120–150 words** · an article, blog post or letter: tell an experience and give your opinion
**120–180 words** · compare two short documents with opposite views (**40–60**), then argue your position (**80–120**)
0–20, from task fulfilment, coherence, vocabulary and grammar
**10/20** (NCLC 7 = 10–11) — aim for 12 in practice for margin
Suspended from 1 Sep 2026 — a 9/20 stays a 9/20

format.title: What the examiners look for
format.body:
**Task fulfilment**: did you do *everything* the prompt asked, for the right reader, within the word range?
**Coherence**: a clear plan, paragraphs, connectors used correctly.
**Vocabulary**: precise words for the topic, nouns with the right gender, no English calques.
**Grammar**: tenses (especially passé composé vs imparfait), agreements, pronouns, a few complex sentences.
A simple, correct, complete text beats an ambitious one full of errors — but at 10+ you also need **some** complex structures (relative clauses, *si* clauses, a subjunctive after *il faut que*).

format.title: Word counts are not optional
format.body:
**Below the minimum**, the task is judged incomplete and the score drops sharply. **Far above the maximum**, you waste time and add errors. Aim for the **middle** of each range: ~90 · ~135 · ~150.
Count as you go: a line of handwriting is roughly 10–12 words. Practise here with the word counter so you learn what 120 words *looks* like.

format.title: Paper or keyboard?
format.body: Depending on the centre, you may write by hand or type. **Check your convocation.** If you'll type, practise typing French accents now (é è à ç ê ô) — losing a minute per paragraph to accents adds up. If by hand, write legibly and leave space to correct.

lessons.title: The three tasks and how they're marked

steps.title: Three genres, three sizes
steps.body:
**T1 — message** (60–120): to one reader, practical, about you.
**T2 — article/blog/letter** (120–150): a story from your life + your opinion, for readers.
**T3 — compare + argue** (120–180): summarise two opposite documents (40–60 words) then give your argued view (80–120).
Each one is graded on **task, coherence, vocabulary, grammar**.

steps.q: Tâche 3 asks for…
options: A short summary of both documents, then your argued opinion
A summary of the first document only
steps.explain: Two parts: the two viewpoints (40–60 words, no opinion yet), then your position with arguments (80–120).

steps.q: Your T2 piece is 98 words. What's the likely consequence?
options: It's under the 120 minimum — the task is judged incomplete and the score drops
It gets a bonus for concision
steps.explain: Below the minimum = task not fulfilled. Aim for ~135 words in T2.

steps.q: Which is the best time split for 60 minutes?
steps.explain: T3 is the longest and hardest to plan; T1 is short. Keep 3–4 minutes at the end of each to proofread.

points: Graded on task, coherence, vocabulary, grammar.
Below the minimum = big penalty. Aim for the middle of each range.

lessons.title: Register: tu or vous, and the right openings

steps.title: Decide the reader before you write a word
steps.body:
**Friend / family** → *tu* · *Salut Marc ! / Coucou !* · *Bises / À bientôt / Je t'embrasse*
**Neighbour, colleague you don't know well** → *vous* · *Bonjour Madame, / Chers voisins,* · *Bien cordialement*
**Manager, company, administration** → *vous* · *Madame, Monsieur,* · *Cordialement* or *Je vous prie d'agréer mes salutations distinguées.*
**Mixing tu and vous in one message is one of the costliest errors** — it breaks task fulfilment.

steps.q: You're writing to your building manager to report a leak. Which opening?
steps.explain: A manager is a formal reader: *vous* and a formal greeting.

steps.q: Which closing matches a message to a close friend?
options: Je vous prie d'agréer mes salutations distinguées.
steps.explain: Formal closings in a friendly message sound strange and cost 'register' marks.

steps.q: Formal: « ___ -vous me rappeler demain ? » (pouvoir, conditional — polite request)
steps.explain: *Pourriez-vous…* is the polite formula for requests to formal readers.

points: Choose the reader → choose tu/vous → keep it **all the way**.
Formal: *Madame, Monsieur,* … *Cordialement*.
Friend: *Salut* … *Bises / À bientôt*.
Polite requests: *Pourriez-vous… ? Je vous serais reconnaissant de…*

steps.title: One shape for every T1
steps.body:
1. **Greeting** (matches the reader)
2. **Why you're writing** — *Je t'écris pour… / Je vous écris pour…*
3. **Two or three details** — who, what, when, where
4. **A request or question** — *Est-ce que tu pourrais… ? Pourriez-vous… ?*
5. **Sign-off**
That's 60–120 words almost automatically. **Answer every part of the prompt**: if it says *describe, invite and give directions*, a missing *directions* is a missing third of the task.

steps.q: Prompt: *Écrivez à un ami pour lui décrire votre nouveau travail et lui proposer de déjeuner ensemble.* Which element is compulsory?
options: Both a description of the job and a lunch invitation
steps.explain: Count the verbs in the prompt: *décrire* + *proposer*. Each is a required part.

steps.q: Which sentence best states the purpose of a message cancelling a meeting?
options: Je vous écris pour vous prévenir que je ne pourrai pas venir à la réunion de jeudi.
Jeudi, il y a une réunion.
steps.explain: Purpose sentence: *Je vous écris pour* + the action + the details (which meeting, when).

steps.q: « Je ___ (pouvoir, futur) pas venir demain. »
steps.explain: *Je ne pourrai pas venir* — future of *pouvoir* is irregular: *pourr-*.

points: Greeting → purpose → 2–3 details → request → sign-off.
Count the verbs in the prompt: each is a required part.
*Je t'écris / Je vous écris pour…* opens every T1.

steps.title: The shape
steps.body:
**Title** → **context** (when, where) → **what happened** → **your reaction** → **opinion + reason + example** → **conclusion / recommendation**.
The story is where tenses are judged: **imparfait** for the scene, background, feelings and habits (*il faisait beau, j'étais stressé*); **passé composé** for the events that move the story (*une voisine m'a présenté, nous avons dansé*).

steps.q: *Quand je ___ (arriver), il ___ (pleuvoir).*
steps.explain: Arriving = event (PC). The rain = background already in progress (imparfait).

steps.q: *Pendant des années, je ___ (se coucher) tard.*
steps.explain: A repeated habit in the past → imparfait.

steps.title: Turning to opinion
steps.body: Mark the turn clearly: *À mon avis, … / Selon moi, … / Je pense que…* + **one reason** (*parce que, car*) + **one example** (*Par exemple, …*). Then a closing line addressed to the readers: *Bref, je conseille à tous de… / N'hésitez pas à…*

steps.q: Which sentence best starts the opinion part?
options: À mon avis, ce type d'événement est essentiel dans les grandes villes, car beaucoup de gens vivent seuls.
steps.explain: Opinion marker + a clear position + a reason, in one sentence.

points: Title → context → events → reaction → opinion + reason + example → close.
Imparfait = scene, feelings, habits · PC = events.
Mark the opinion clearly: *À mon avis / Selon moi*.

lessons.title: Tâche 3: summarise without copying, then argue

steps.title: Part 1 (40–60 words): report, don't copy
steps.body:
Present **both** documents neutrally, **in your own words**. Useful reporting verbs: *Le premier document affirme / défend / présente… · Le second, en revanche, souligne / estime / met en garde contre…*
Copying whole sentences from the documents is penalised. Change the structure: noun → verb, positive → negative, a synonym.

steps.q: Document: *« Le télétravail améliore la qualité de vie : moins de trajets. »* Best reformulation?
options: Selon le premier document, travailler de chez soi permet de passer moins de temps dans les transports.
Le premier document dit : « Le télétravail améliore la qualité de vie : moins de trajets. »
steps.explain: Same idea, new words and structure, and it attributes the view (*Selon le premier document*).

steps.title: Part 2 (80–120 words): take a side, then nuance
steps.body:
*Pour ma part, je pense que…* (clear position) → **argument 1 + example** → **argument 2** → **concession** (*Certes…, mais…*) → **conclusion** (*En somme, … / Ainsi, …*).
A nuanced position is fine (*à condition que…*), but it must be **a position**. Sitting on the fence (*les deux ont raison*) with no conclusion scores low.

steps.q: Which is a real position?
options: Pour ma part, je suis favorable au télétravail, à condition qu'il ne dépasse pas trois jours par semaine.
Les deux documents ont des arguments intéressants.
steps.explain: It takes a side and adds a condition. The others describe without deciding.

steps.q: « Je suis favorable à cette mesure, à condition qu'elle ___ (être) bien expliquée. »
steps.explain: *À condition que* + subjunctive: *qu'elle soit*.

points: Part 1: both views, neutral, **own words**, 40–60 words.
Part 2: position → 2 arguments + example → *Certes…, mais…* → conclusion.
Nuance is good; no position is bad.
Watch **both** word limits.

steps.title: Twelve that do most of the work
steps.body:
**Order:** d'abord · ensuite · enfin
**Add:** de plus · en outre
**Cause:** parce que · car · grâce à (+) · à cause de (–)
**Consequence:** donc · c'est pourquoi · ainsi
**Contrast:** mais · cependant · en revanche · pourtant
**Concession:** certes… mais · bien que + subjonctif · même si + indicatif
**Example:** par exemple · notamment
**Conclude:** en somme · bref · pour conclure
Use **different** ones: *mais, mais, mais* shows a narrow range.

steps.q: *Il a réussi ___ son travail régulier.* (positive cause)
steps.explain: *Grâce à* = thanks to (positive). *À cause de* is for negative causes.

steps.q: *___ il pleuve, nous sortirons.*
steps.explain: *Bien que* + subjunctive (*pleuve*). *Même s'il pleut* would need the indicative.

steps.q: Which connector introduces an opposite idea?
steps.explain: *En revanche* = on the other hand. *De plus* adds; *ainsi* concludes.

points: Vary connectors — range is graded.
*grâce à* (+) vs *à cause de* (–).
*bien que* + subjunctive · *même si* + indicative.
*en revanche / cependant / pourtant* for contrast.

lessons.title: The last 3 minutes: proofread for points

steps.title: A 7-point check
steps.body:
Keep 3 minutes per task to check, in this order:
1. **Every part** of the prompt answered?
2. **Word count** inside the range?
3. **tu/vous** consistent?
4. **Gender** of every noun + adjective agreement
5. **PC vs imparfait** and **être** verbs (*je suis allé(e)*)
6. **depuis + present** · *si* + present/imparfait (never conditional after *si*)
7. **Accents** on the common words: *à, où, déjà, très, été, après*.

steps.q: Spot the error: *Si j'aurais le temps, je viendrais.*
steps.explain: Never conditional after *si*: *Si j'avais… je viendrais*.

steps.q: Spot the error: *J'habite à Lagos depuis cinq ans et j'ai travaillé ici depuis deux ans.*
options: je travaille ici depuis deux ans
steps.explain: *Depuis* + an ongoing situation = present tense.

steps.q: Spot the error: *Ma famille et moi, nous avons allés au marché.*
steps.explain: *Aller* takes *être* in the passé composé.

points: Proofread 3 minutes per task — it's the cheapest score in the exam.
Check: parts · words · tu/vous · gender · PC/imp · depuis & si · accents.
Log every error you find in your **error log**.

mistakes.title: Missing part of the prompt
mistakes.why: The prompt asks to describe AND invite; you only describe. Task fulfilment drops a band.
mistakes.fix: Underline every verb in the prompt and tick each one off your plan.

mistakes.title: Below the minimum word count
mistakes.why: An incomplete task can't score well however good the French.
mistakes.fix: Aim for the middle: ~90 / ~135 / ~150. Practise with the counter until you know the length by sight.

mistakes.title: Mixing tu and vous
mistakes.why: Register is part of task fulfilment.
mistakes.fix: Decide the reader first; check tu/vous in the final proofread.

mistakes.title: Tense errors in the story (T2)
mistakes.why: PC vs imparfait is graded hardest in T2.
mistakes.fix: Imparfait = scene/feelings/habits; PC = events. Drill the PC/imparfait trap.

mistakes.title: Copying the documents in T3
mistakes.why: Copied sentences show no language of your own — and may not be counted.
mistakes.fix: Reformulate: new structure, synonyms, reporting verbs (*affirme, souligne, estime*).

mistakes.title: No clear position in T3
mistakes.why: *Les deux ont raison* without a conclusion reads as avoiding the task.
mistakes.fix: *Pour ma part, je pense que…* in the first line of part 2 — nuance after.

mistakes.title: Conditional after si
mistakes.why: *Si j'aurais* is a very visible error at B1–B2.

mistakes.title: English calques and faux amis
mistakes.fix: Drill the faux-amis trap; keep a personal list in your error log.

checklist: Read the prompt twice; **underline every verb** — each is a required part.
Decide the **reader** → tu or vous → greeting and sign-off.
Write the plan in 1 minute (the template for that task).
Watch the clock: T1 ≈ 15 min, T2 ≈ 20, T3 ≈ 25.
Aim for the middle of each word range.
Keep 3 minutes per task to proofread: parts · words · tu/vous · gender · tenses · si/depuis · accents.
